gen-gf-cabin-sketch-roboto-slab: Bold, marker-tip letters give Cabin Sketch a hand-drawn stoutness, like pipe cleaner strokes. Roboto Slab, a slab-serif, is more structured, its open throats keeping the middle of each line dominant; shrink the heading and that drawn character fades fast.
gen-gf-cactus-classical-serif-fs-bespoke: Bespoke Sans reads sharp and refined, with generous space where its curves stop short of the stem, while Cactus Classical Serif adds gentle weight variation above. Paragraphs would move along smoothly.
gen-gf-cagliostro-fs-literata: Plain and contemporary, Cagliostro keeps its lines low in contrast, while Literata's sturdy hairlines and slightly heavier thick strokes bring a bookish warmth. Cagliostro is best at stating things; Literata, at carrying them.
gen-gf-cairo-fs-literata: Crisp and modern, Cairo spaces its letters wide enough that even tiny sizes stay sharp. Literata, a serif, then adds comfortable thick and thin variation, with curved letters opening wide for a bookish texture underneath.
gen-gf-caladea-fs-bespoke-sans: Dignified and bookish, Caladea shows only a modest gap between its stems and hairlines, which Bespoke Sans meets with low contrast and generous space beside each stem. Sharp, refined sans lines sit under a serif heading without competing.
gen-gf-cambay-fs-literata: Cambay opens the pair with approachable, modern curves whose endings never get near each other. And Literata, a text serif, carries a longer read with moderate thick and thin strokes and wide, unclosed mouths.
gen-gf-cantarell-fs-literata: Gaping curves and a steady, marker-like line weight mark Cantarell as unmistakable. Literata follows with a serif texture, its thin strokes about half the weight of the thick ones, adding bookish sophistication.
gen-gf-cantata-one-fs-bespoke-sans: Classic and editorial, Cantata One sets its wide-set letters on ink-heavy verticals with thread-like diagonals. And Bespoke Sans, a plain sans, stays low in contrast, so a longer passage would read sharp and refined.
gen-gf-cantora-one-fs-literata: Literata is sophisticated and bookish, with sturdy hairlines and curved letters whose mouths stay wide open. Literata sits well under Cantora One, whose modern flow of stroke thickness leaves the heading light and unfussy.
gen-gf-capriola-fs-literata: Literata reads bookish and sophisticated, with wide, unclosed curves. Capriola, plain and approachable in a low-contrast sans, sits above it while Literata's text serif strokes land at a comfortable midpoint between flat and dramatic.
